scope: Seeded yen native-weight and placement development repair, not a held-out trial.

meaning.evidence: In the enlarged vectors of both proofs I see a coin ring enclosing two diagonal arms that converge into a vertical stem crossed by two horizontal bars — an unambiguous ¥ coin. The nearest plausible confusion is the ₩ in the reference strip, but the candidate has a single converged stem rather than the won's two descending legs, so the reading holds.

style.evidence: Ring stroke weight, flat terminals on the V-arm tips and bar ends, and the ~55% glyph-to-diameter proportion match the ₺/₱/₩ references, including the references' habit of drawing crossbars slightly lighter than the ring (compare the candidate's crossbars at rows 8/10 with the peso's twin bars).

optics.evidence: At 16px/1x the inter-bar counter is fully open on both paints (outlined row 9 x5,x6=255,255 and x9,x10=255,255; filled row 9 x21,x22=0,0 and x25,x26=0,0), and the V fork stays open across rows 4–5 (outlined x6–x9 at 237–255; filled x23,x24=18). The weakest feature is the stem below the lower bar (outlined row 11 = 143, filled row 11 = 109, ~44% coverage) — dim but rendered on both surfaces and fully solid at 2x, so not a collapse.

family.evidence: The two paints share concept, diameter and layout exactly: both occupy rows 1–14, and the crossbars sit at rows 8/10 spanning x5–x10 outlined and x21–x26 filled (the same columns after the 16px strip offset). The only differences are the deliberate ring-vs-disc inversion and its expected antialiasing polarity.

findings.message: e1 and e3 are 0.25px apart; minimum is 1px. Move them apart or knock one out of the other.
